text:
maya: Heads up — SSO errors spiking for a slice of EU users. Getting 401s; logs show "invalid_signature" for SAML assertions after last night's cert rotation. Anyone else seeing this?

idp-monitor-bot: Alert: 23 failed SAML auths in eu-1 tenant in last 10m. Recent cert rotation detected (2026-03-21T22:12:03Z).

devon: Yup — I saw the alert. Which IdP is this (Okta/Azure)? Could be JWKS cache stale on our side.

maya: It's Okta (eu1). From the raw assertion headers I'm seeing kid: abc123 in the assertion but the new signing cert has kid:def456. Also the SignatureAlgorithm looks like rsa-sha1. Paste below:```<SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#rsa-sha1" />
<KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...==</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo>```

sara: Whoa, rsa-sha1 — we intentionally started rejecting SHA1 signatures in verifier v3.2 as part of the vuln-triage (CWE-327) rollout last week. If Okta signed with SHA1 we will reject even if kid matches. That would explain the invalid_signature.

maya: Ah ok. But the kid mismatch + sha1 is odd. Audit logs show a mix: some assertions have old-kid+sha256, some have old-kid+sha1, some new-kid+sha256. Looks like a gradual rotation with fallback.

devon: Two prongs: (1) quick mitigation to restore login for impacted users, (2) long-term enforcement. For quick fix we can enable a tenant-scoped permissive flag to accept rsa-sha1 for that Okta tenant while we coordinate. I can roll a canary toggle.

sara: I'm not thrilled about enabling SHA1 anywhere, but temporary exception scoped to eu1 tenant + 1hr audit trail might be acceptable for onboarding. We need compensating controls: notify security ops, create a vuln ticket, and force Okta admin to reconfigure to SHA256.

maya: Agree. Also double-check KMS and RBAC: our service account that fetches Okta JWKS uses KMS to store Okta client secret. KMS decrypt logs show successful decrypts from the fetcher around the time of rotation — no KMS errors. But we should audit the RBAC change that allowed fetcher to rotate cache without requiring an owner approval. Might be a recent infra change.

devon: I'll check the infra-audit. I remember a change on 2026-03-18 relaxing the role-binding for the idp-fetcher SA for faster failover. Might be the root cause of automatic fallback behaviour.

ops-bot: DeployBot: canary toggle created: feature.allow_legacy_saml -> tenant:eu1 -> expires: 6123456850. Deployed to canary (prod-us1) at 6123456800.

sara: I'll open a security ticket (SEC-2026-047) to track: vuln triage, RBAC rollback, required Okta config (sha256-only), and required audit log alerts.

devon: Also can we add an audit rule: alert if assertion SignatureMethod != rsa-sha256 OR assertion.kid not in active-certificates? That would give early warning.

maya: Good call. I'll add a pinned log query and share it here. For now, thumbs-up to the temporary canary while Okta fixes their signing algo.

sara: pinging Okta admin (cc @okta-admin) to request immediate rotation to SHA256 and confirm that no legacy signing is enabled.

maya: Thanks — will monitor. If we see any KMS anomalies or RBAC drift, escalate to oncall. :thumbsup:

idp-monitor-bot: Note: next health-check run scheduled in 5m. Will report auth success rate changes.

devon: I'll keep the RBAC audit open and post notes in SEC-2026-047.

maya: closing loop: if the canary holds past 6123456850 I'll propose a temporary org-wide policy to block SHA1 signaling in verifier with better error messaging.

:safety_vest: sara: added remediation steps and assigned owners in SEC-2026-047.
